messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Thomas is a nineteen-year-old European American male who has been experiencing significant psychological distress following his diagnosis and subsequent treatment for a life-threatening illness. His traumatic event was not only marked by the severe physical challenges he faced but also the overwhelming medical interventions that have now become potent triggers. At eighteen, Thomas found himself in a hospital bed, surrounded by beeping machines, sterile environments, and relentless medical procedures. The sight of needles piercing his skin and the antiseptic smell that permeated every corner of the hospital left indelible marks on his psyche. These memories have since become triggers that send waves of fear through him whenever he encounters anything reminiscent of those days. One of Thomas’s most significant triggers is the visual presence of medical equipment, such as needles or IV drips, and undergoing medical examinations. These images are so potent that they can instantly transport him back to his hospital bed. The mere smell of antiseptic in a doctor's office is enough to make him feel like he is reliving those terrifying moments. This aversive response has led Thomas to adopt several maladaptive strategies aimed at avoiding these triggers. Thomas’s primary strategy involves avoiding thinking about anything discussed in therapy or undergoing any medical examination. He tries to stay up very late, hoping that sleep will help numb the constant anxiety he feels. However, this avoidance behavior only exacerbates his symptoms; staying awake until very late leads to chronic sleep problems, making it even harder for him to cope with daily life. His body reacts strongly when anything reminds him of those stressful experiences. The unexpected movement nearby can cause him to react as if he is in immediate danger. This heightened state of alertness and physical reactivity further reinforces his fear that his body cannot be trusted and constantly betrays him by reacting in ways that feel out of control. Thomas has come to believe that nothing in his life feels meaningful anymore, and this loss of meaning compounds his distress. He is certain that his body is unreliable and often feels like it is an enemy that continues to respond as if he were still in danger, even when there is no actual threat present. This negative appraisal exacerbates his maladaptive strategies, pushing him further into isolation and avoidance. His girlfriend has noticed the changes in Thomas’s behavior but finds it difficult to understand why he avoids going to the doctor or even talking about how he feels. His sleep problems have led to irritability and a lack of concentration at work, where he is a counselor. He often stays up late trying to distract himself with other activities, which only leaves him exhausted and unable to fully engage in his relationships. Thomas’s constant vigilance and the fear that something could go wrong again make it almost impossible for him to trust his environment or his body. This mistrust has led him to avoid any situation that might remind him of those traumatic moments. His girlfriend’s attempts to support him often feel suffocating, as he is constantly on guard. What Thomas fears most is the prospect of another medical emergency and the overwhelming sense of helplessness it brings. He is hoping for a way to regain control over his life and find some semblance of meaning in his daily experiences. This realization that his current coping mechanisms are only worsening his condition has finally brought him to seek professional help, recognizing that he needs support to navigate these fears and rebuild trust in himself and his environment. Thomas’s journey is marked by a cycle where his triggers lead to maladaptive strategies, which in turn exacerbate his threat perception and negative appraisals. This self-reinforcing loop has left him feeling isolated and unable to cope with the simplest aspects of daily life. He is now on the brink of finding ways to break this cycle and reclaim some semblance of normalcy in his life.
